The <3,3,3> tensor lies on the 20th secant variety of the Segre embedding but only via a second-order contact (osculating) scheme: the tensor is a limit of 21 rank-1 terms where two of the terms coalesce along distinct tangent directions of the Segre variety. Resolving a k-th order osculating degeneration into an exact decomposition requires replacing the osculating point with (k+1) rank-1 terms \u2014 the base term plus k terms for the tangent directions. Since the border-rank-21 witness uses a second-order (k=2) degeneration, the minimum exact rank along this degeneration path is 21 - 2 + (2+1) = 22... but the specific bilinear structure of matrix multiplication forces the two osculating directions to be linearly independent in a way that requires one additional 'cross' term to cancel interference, pushing the floor to 23. The Laderman decomposition achieves exactly this bound.
